# Salt and acid

Most dishes that taste flat need salt, and most that taste heavy need acid. I season in layers: a pinch with the onions, a pinch with the liquid, a final adjustment at the table. Lemon juice, vinegar or a spoon of yoghurt lifts a stew just before serving.

Tasting constantly is the habit that matters. A clean spoon for every taste, a glass of water between dishes. If a sauce is bitter, a little sugar or fat rounds it; if it is sharp, salt softens it. Pickles and ferments bring their own acidity, so reduce the salt elsewhere.

Write down the final amounts once a recipe works, because memory is unreliable.
